title: Characterizing digraph support families by rooted-interval deletion
abstract: We answer the set-theoretic characterization question for digraph support families posed by Mike Steel in Section 4 of Interior operators and their relationship to autocatalytic networks (arXiv:2305.16714v4, 2023). A digraph on a finite set E is given by a predecessor map P assigning to each vertex e a set P(e) of in-neighbours, loops allowed, and a set S is supported when every element e of S has some element of S in P(e). The characterization refers only to the family F. Start from the full power set of E with no roots used. A legal step chooses a remaining set S outside F that is inclusion-maximal among the remaining sets outside F, chooses a root r in S that has not been used before and lies in no member of F contained in S, and deletes every remaining set X with r in X and X contained in S. A family F of subsets of E is exactly the support family of some predecessor map on E if and only if some finite sequence of legal steps ends exactly at F.
